narrative: Demand for PL1__MCCF3FA4 is smooth with CV=0.43 and a statistically significant declining trend (slope=-6.97, p=0.0073). Lead time is unstable (CV=0.68), making it the dominant driver of safety stock requirements. A (r,Q) continuous-review policy with SS=9910 and OQ=6062 (EOQ-based) achieves 95% service level at 77.4% capacity utilisation, reducing annual costs by 96.3% versus the current SAP configuration.
warnings: Declining demand trend detected (p=0.0073) — review forecast quarterly
Lead time is unstable (CV=0.68) — monitor supplier performance continuously

research_insights.selection_rationale: The (r,Q) model is optimal for this material: demand is smooth and near-normally distributed (CV=0.43), volume is high (~5,661 units/day), and lead times, while variable, are short (<2.5 days effective). EOQ minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs given the large gap between unit cost * holding rate and ordering cost. The fixed OQ of 6,062 units balances replenishment frequency against holding cost efficiently.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Reorder point (22,985) structurally exceeds max storage (20,624) as a trigger level — this is not a post-replenishment capacity breach (SS+OQ=15,972 <= 20,624). However, the declining demand trend means ROP should be recalculated quarterly to avoid inflating cycle-stock and breaching capacity in practice.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Declining demand trend (p=0.0073, slope=-6.97 units/day) requires quarterly policy review; lead time CV=0.68 requires active supplier monitoring.
